title: Figma announces new features to define how agents work on its platform
slides: Can Figma control how AI agents design?
New features aim to define agent behavior on the platform
Agents might soon edit files without human approval
Designers must learn to set boundaries for agent actions
Start defining your agent rules before they act
thread_text:
1. Agents Don't Ask Permission

Figma is rolling out features that let AI design agents edit files autonomously—no human approval required. That's a real shift in how work gets done on the platform.

2. New Rules for Agent Behavior

Figma is adding controls so teams can define what agents can and can't do. You'll be able to set guardrails before an agent touches a single layer.

3. One Click, Zero Oversight

If an agent can edit without approval, a small mistake can cascade across dozens of files. The speed gain is real—so is the risk of silent changes.

4. Designers as Boundary Setters

The skill isn't just designing anymore. It's deciding which actions agents can take alone and which need a human check. That's a new part of the job.

5. Set Rules Before Agents Act

Open Figma today and draft a simple permission list: what can an agent edit, move, or delete without asking? Share it with your team this week. Does your current workflow already assume agents will ask first?
